newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat, Israeli in crisis talks with Egyptians.
newsitem.headline: Arafat, Israeli in crisis talks with Egyptians.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and an envoy from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu crossed paths on Thursday in Cairo, the centre of Arab consultations on the crisis in Middle East peace talks.
Arab ministers who visited Cairo earlier in the day said Israel was killing the peace process, especially by starting to build more Jewish housing in mainly Arab East Jerusalem.
Arafat and Israeli envoy Dore Gold flew into the Egyptian capital separately just as the Syrian and Lebanese ministers were leaving after talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
Gold, Netanyahu's foreign policy adviser, told reporters: "I'm here to convey a message from Israel to Egypt and we have a very new proposal about the peace process to discuss."
He was apparently referring to Netanyahu's offer to complete the "final status" talks within six months, nearly two years earlier than planned.

The Palestinians have dismissed the plan as a trick. In the latest reaction, Palestinian negotiator Nabil Shaath said their priority was to stop the Israelis building settlements such as the new one at Jebel Abu Ghenim, or Hor Homa, in East Jerusalem.
"Why is it that the Israelis try to sell us things that have been sold several times before?" he said of the proposal.

"What is important is that they implement what has been agreed upon and immediately stop the process of settlements and building in Jerusalem so that we can proceed forward to the "final status" negotiations because we can't begin with his (Netanyahu's) bulldozers and tanks," he added.
Shaath said the Palestinians would knock on every door in their diplomatic campaign but would not use violence to protest at the new settlement that Israel started building this week.

"We are going to use all the political rules available to us. We will do our best to keep utilising the political roles when there is an opportunity -- from the Islamic summit in Pakistan to the Jerusalem summit in Rabat to a proposed Arab summit, again and again to the Security Council," he said.

Asked about clashes in Bethlehem on Thursday between Israeli troops and Palestinians protesting against the Jerusalem settlement, he said: "We are using peaceful protest, the Israeli army shoots at peaceful demonstrators."
Officials said Arafat would see Mubarak, while Gold would have talks with Mubarak's foreign policy adviser, Osama el-Baz.

After Mubarak's talks earlier with Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara and Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, in one of the strongest statements on the crisis, said Israel could not expect to go on tricking the Arabs with fine-sounding promises.

Shara told a news conference with Moussa that he felt Arabs were moving towards serious commitment to the Cairo summit agreement of last year. The summit made an implicit threat to suspend normal relations with Israel.

"Don't underestimate Arab intelligence and don't play games with us," Moussa added in an address aimed at Israeli leaders. "We cannot be deceived with any shining and sugar-coated promises...the weight of which we know," he added.

The Egyptian minister said the Oslo agreement between Israel and the Palestinians clearly said the status of Jerusalem was for negotiation and that no one should take unilateral measures there -- an argument that the Israeli government rejects.

Israel considers Jerusalem -- the Arab eastern half of which was captured in the 1967 Middle East war -- to be its undivided capital. But Palestinians view the eastern part as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
"This means settlements and it means no steps in Jerusalem. No state will accept anything other than that. They have to understand that and that's what they will be told," he added.

"He (Netanyahu) is intelligent, no doubt, and we don't accuse him of being anything else. But we want him to have enough sensitivity and understand that he is not the only decision-maker," Moussa said.
